## [v8.0.0-rc.7](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/v8.0.0-rc.7)
*GitHub Releases · Prisma* | 25/08/2026 | Score: 0.70
Tags: creative_workflow

> <h1>v8.0.0-rc.7</h1> <p>ORM collection pagination renames to <code>limit</code>/<code>offset</code>, and the toolchain releases against <code>@prisma/cli-engine@0.2.3</code>, the engine whose config loader ships the <code>prisma init</code> scaffold fixes from the unified CLI's rc line.</p> <p>The upgrade recipe for this hop: the <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/tree/v8.0.0-rc.7/skills/prisma-8/upgrading/app/upgrades/8.0.0-rc.6-to-8.0.0-rc.7/">user recipe</a>.</p> <h2>Breaking changes</h2> <ul> <li> <p><strong>ORM pagination is <code>limit</code>/<code>offset</code>, not <code>take</code>/<code>skip</code></strong> — <code>.take(n)</code> and <code>.skip(n)</code> are renamed to <code>.limit(n)</code> and <code>.offset(n)</code> on SQL and Mongo ORM collections, including relation refinements and grouped SQL collections; the old names are removed. Semantics are unchanged. Mongo's lower-level query builder keeps <code>.skip(n)</code> — it names the native <code>$skip</code> pipeline stage, not the collection API. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/30112" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/30112/hovercard">#30112</a>)</p> <p>Before:</p> <div class="highlight
